stories.title: How a tree in Hanoi points to flowering of dissent among Vietnam’s Gen Z
stories.summary: A tree in Hanoi has become a symbol of how Vietnam’s Gen Z views its country – but it is not the enviable growth story sold by the government. Tree 55 on Nguyen Huy Tu Street – now dubbed the “Justice Tree” – was buried under bouquets earlier this month. It was an act of digital-age defiance over the death of a teenager in a road traffic accident in the area that went unpunished. Response to the accident, which triggered a belated explanation from the state, reveals unease with a system many...

stories.title: South African airline defends low-altitude aerial stunt over packed stadium
stories.summary: The South African airline behind a dramatic stunt that saw two of its aircraft in close formation fly reportedly within feet of the top of a stadium has defended itself in the face of some criticism. The jets roared over Cape Town's DHL stadium as flares shot up before the start of a rugby match featuring fierce rivals South Africa and New Zealand. Some labelled the manoeuvre reckless, while others have praised the precision and expertise required to pull it off. In response, Airlink said it was carefully planned with the support of the aviation authorities. "Planning. Precision. Performance," was the airline's message in social media posts, external accompanied by the footage. In a statement reproduced on a government news site, external, Airlink went into more detail. "The two aircraft were flown by highly experienced crew, with each comprised of three senior captains operating in the roles of commander, co-pilot and safety/technical officer," the airline said. It added that the flights were performed with the "approved and rehearsed safety altitude and speed limits for the flypast". The flight tracking website Flightradar24, external said that according to its analysis "the lead aircraft passed less than 50 feet (15 metres) above the top of the stadium". Questions have been raised over the risk and potential for disaster involving two planes and a packed stadium, but many South Africans have responded with expressions of national pride that its country's pilots could pull this off.
